name: Victor

systems.flavorDescription: The often maligned Anticipatory Reactor Shielding is a controversial system frequently used by more reckless pilots. While undoubtedly effective at reducing excess reactor heat to 0, the actual use case often deteriorates into guess work on the pilots part as surrounding parameters exponentially increase with each reactor surge. As any user error results in further heat build up, the system's downsides become apparent to most potential users.

"Last Gamble" is a volatile virus capable of wreaking havoc with circuitry and other delicate systems, potentially propagating and reducing a frame to a slumped over smoldering wreck. Application of the virus is the main concern. Unable to be spread digitally via the omninet, for it could be potent enough to eradicate every single connected device in the immediate vicinity to scrap metal, a different delivery method is required. The moments following its analog delivery are often tense, though over in microseconds. The more damage the user intends to inflict on the target the more a backfire of Last Gamble becomes likely. The Unleashed virus surges through the paths of least resistance, obliterating all circuitry in its way, which, if proper calculations were neglected, may very well be the user's systems instead of the targets.

Insidious scrambling of both targeting and motor control software can seriously hamper any enemy. While usually hard to accomplish with conventional malware, the Misfortune Casino program is tying the outcome to targeted, falsified objectives in a frame's data core. By presenting the system a way out in this manner, it becomes easier to manipulate its underlying, fundamental routines.

[let’s sit a while, and think on things to come]
Gained from the Technophile: Rank III pilot talent.
By installing additional armor plating, redundant firing circuits, and enhanced insulation to magazines the longevity of a frame’s armaments can be greatly enhanced.

weapon.flavorDescription: "Schrödinger's Rifle" as it is more colloquially known by the Lancers that use it, is a marvel of applied Quantum Mechanics and energy transformation. Appearing as a heavy energy rifle on the surface, the QSR is special in that it is able to carry a theoretically infinite amount of charges within its specialized Quantum Reactor. While this theory may not hold up in reality, opponents staring down a sustained onslaught of fire from this weapon eventually have to ask themselves "Do I feel lucky?" as each squeeze of the trigger may or may not unload the weapon entirely, an outcome which is only observable following the engagement of the next firing cycle.

bondPowers.name: Stroke of Luck
bondPowers.description: When you fail a skill check and take Stress, put yourself into danger, or seriously mess up, tell the GM you stumble onto something lucky of their choice a way forward, an opportunity, or a lucky break. You or another character gain +1 Accuracy on the next check acting on this stroke of luck.

bondPowers.name: Heart of Hearts
bondPowers.description: When you and your group are in a tough spot, you can flash back to a scene from your past or hometown and describe how your memory of that time inspires you in the current moment. You can treat your next roll as though you rolled an unmodified 20. You can only ever use this ability three times; after that, replace it with a new power from this bond.

bondAnswers: A stubborn refusal to give up.
minorIdeal: Someone else helped me out of a bad situation.

armor.flavorDescription: The heaviest hardsuits. They are always powered and up-armored with thick, composite armor. Heavy hardsuits often feature integrated weapons, powerful mobility suites, and – by augmenting their user’s strength – allow their user to field much heavier weapons than normal infantry can typically carry. Heavy hardsuits are in decline now that half-size chassis are popular, but they are still common among private militaries and middle-tier Diasporan armed forces.

weapons.flavorDescription: Medium A/C weapons are typically swords, officer’s sabers, and trench axes.
Light A/C weapons might be knives, bayonets, punching daggers, and short swords.

gear.flavorDescription: Small, non-combat drones are a common sight in the field. They’re fairly noisy but can fly about half a mile with good maneuverability before losing signal, relaying audio and visual information as they go.
“Patch” is pilot slang for any kind of modern first aid gear, including sprayable medi-gel and instant-acting medical patches.

A powered third arm mounted on a bracket on the hardsuit. Tertiary arms are powered and controlled using the same neural bridge processes that allow hardsuits to respond to user input. They can be equipped with manipulators to allow for fine motor control, weapons to enhance combat efficacy, or specialty tools.
